description: Reviewed starter scenarios shipped with Maintainer-Zero.

scenarios.title: CI and release outage
scenarios.summary: Simulate verification and release pipelines becoming unavailable.

trigger.description: CI cannot validate or publish changes during the drill window.

assumptions: Workflow files are evidence of a pipeline, not proof that a backup runner exists.
The repository can use a documented local validation fallback.

inputs.name: release_files
inputs.description: Release configuration paths found in the repository.

recovery_actions: Document local test and release commands.
Record a reviewed backup runner and credential handoff path.
limitations: Does not call GitHub APIs or verify runner availability.
Does not execute workflows or publish a release.

scenarios.title: Dependency yanked
scenarios.summary: Simulate a declared dependency becoming unavailable to a clean build.

trigger.description: A dependency source no longer serves a package needed by a clean install.

assumptions: Names in supported manifests approximate the dependency surface.
A listed dependency is not proof that the package is currently unavailable.

inputs.name: dependencies
inputs.description: Normalized dependency names from supported manifests.

inputs.name: cold_build
inputs.description: Whether a clean, network-isolated build was verified.

score.formula: 100 when no supported dependency is declared; otherwise 100 minus a bounded dependency-surface penalty

recovery_actions: Pin sources and versions and retain a reviewed fallback mirror.
Schedule a clean-build check without warm caches.
limitations: Does not contact package indexes or prove that a package was yanked.
Only currently supported manifest formats are considered.

scenarios.title: Core maintainer unavailable
scenarios.summary: Simulate a high-contribution maintainer becoming unavailable during the drill.

trigger.description: The highest-contribution maintainer cannot review, merge, or release changes.

assumptions: Commit concentration is a proxy for work capacity, not a measure of individual worth.
A CODEOWNER rule does not prove that the listed person is available.

inputs.name: contributors
inputs.description: Contributor commit counts from local Git history.

inputs.name: release_files
inputs.description: Release configuration paths found in the repository.

score.formula: weighted backup-maintainer, CODEOWNERS, and release-path signals, bounded to 0..100

recovery_actions: Assign a second owner for each critical path and verify access.
Practice a review, merge, and release handoff with a clean checkout.
limitations: Commit history cannot establish current availability or permissions.
The backlog model is deterministic and is not calibrated incident probability.
